text.p: Domtar Inc on Monday confirmed it proposed to Avenor Inc's board a friendly merger of Domtar, Avenor and Repap Enterprises.
The rejected proposal contemplated that the three companies would enter into a merger agreement prior to the vote on the Avenor/Repap merger scheduled for March 26.

Domtar said the combination would have created one of the leading global competitors in the paper and forest products industry, with combined 1996 revenues of C$5.2 billion and assets of C$7.8 billion.

Domtar President and Chief Executive Officer Raymond Royer held meetings with Avenor's senior officials to discuss Domtar's proposal. Avenor management, after reviewing the matter with the company's board, advised Domtar that they would not pursue this proposal, Domtar said.

"We had hoped that, by adding Domtar's complementary businesses, management and strong balance sheet to this mix, we would have allayed the concerns of Avenor's shareholders," Royer said in a statement.
"I still believe that a negotiated agreement between the three companies before the vote would provide significant opportunities to improve shareholder value of all three companies."
